findings.reason: §1's premise (the shared paths are the record's home) and §2's rule are both superseded, and §2 must be rewritten against the fragment design or it rebuilds machinery the code has removed.
findings.text: §2 grants every implement, test and investigate node the plan file, the plan's cumulative evidence record and a figures directory, but `_landing_fragment_paths` has given each node its own fragment (docs/evidence/fragments/<plan>/<node-id>.html and docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/) by default since commit f6e41cc7d, and `_shared_landing_paths` records that the shared grant was deliberately removed because "a grant every node holds is exactly the merge conflict the per-node fragment default removes" — so §2 as written would regress the shipped design and re-open the merge-conflict this plan's §1 argues against

findings.reason: §4 should be reduced to the figure-verification twins and the vision-lane decision, since the deliverable contract it proposes to write already exists.
findings.text: §4 instructs that the contract text "names the figure as a deliverable with a topic directory, a statement of what it shows, and the plotting rules", but `PLAN_LANDING_CONTRACT` already carries that text ("Use a figure wherever a spatial, plotted or sequential relationship is clearer shown than described, under your own docs/figures/<plan>/<node-id>/ ... never an image of what is naturally a table"), so §4's first half is already shipped and only the verification and vision-lane half remains

findings.reason: the design should be stated as an edit to those owners rather than a parallel scope path that would drift from the fragment grant and the read-only-role withholding rule they already encode.
findings.text: §2 would add a second computation of plan-file, evidence-record and figure-directory paths for a node's write scope beside `_shared_landing_paths` (line 1967) and `_landing_fragment_paths` (line 2023), which already own that resolution and feed `_grant_landing_write_paths`, `_writes_its_landing_fragment` and the contract composer

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan introduces no new module; it extends the existing deep owners in place (reckon/crew/dispatch.py for scope and the dispatch refusal, reckon/crew/promotion.py for the completion gate).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2 adds a second resolution of the same three landing paths beside the owner at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1967 that already computes exactly those paths for a node's scope.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 re-proposes a default grant of the plan file, the plan's cumulative evidence record and a figures directory that reckon/crew/dispatch.py already resolves, and which a later change replaced with a per-node fragment default.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §3's `--no-record REASON` extends the existing `--no-commit` override on the same function rather than wrapping it, and no other surface is a pass-through layer.
